target.description: Six pure, in-memory CSS color tools: parse, convert, WCAG/APCA contrast, gamut map, ramps, solver

checks.summary: Listed in the MCP Registry as io.github.aimsise/color-engine-mcp.
Repository owner matches GitHub namespace aimsise.

observation.network_policy: sinkhole: DNS is answered with placeholder addresses and every TCP connection and UDP datagram is captured inside the sandbox; nothing leaves it

tools.name: parse_color
tools.description: Parse a CSS color string and return hex, rgb, oklch, and gamut info.

tools.name: convert_color
tools.description: Convert a CSS color string into a canonical hex, rgb, hsl, or oklch format string.

tools.name: contrast
tools.description: Compute the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio between two fully opaque CSS color strings and return WCAG tier flags (AA/AAA normal/large text). Set apca:true to also get the signed APCA-W3 Lc for text `a` over background `b`.

tools.name: gamut_map
tools.description: Map any CSS color string into the sRGB gamut via perceptual OKLCH chroma reduction. Returns the nearest in-gamut hex, raw OKLCH components, and a `clamped` flag indicating whether the input was out-of-gamut.

tools.name: generate_ramp
tools.description: Generate a tint-to-shade color ramp from a base CSS color. Returns an ordered list of swatches (light → dark) each with its in-gamut hex, display-rounded OKLCH components (l/c 5dp, h 2dp), WCAG contrast ratios (2dp) + tiers vs white and black, and an in-gamut flag. Optionally emits the ramp as design tokens via tokenFormat ("tailwind" JSON or a "css-variables" :root block).

tools.name: solve_for_contrast
tools.description: Find a foreground color that meets one or more WCAG 2.1 contrast targets against a background. Binary-searches OKLCH lightness (holding hue/chroma fixed) and returns the nearest-compliant hex plus the achieved ratio. Pass `target` for one target or `targets` for several; `prefer` selects lighter/darker/either; `hue`/`chroma` pin the foreground chromaticity. If BOTH `target` and `targets` are provided, `targets` takes precedence. The response shape differs by mode: a single `target` returns `{ met, color, ratio }` (with an optional `nearMiss` flag); `targets` returns `{ results: [{ met, color,

sandbox: Network: container namespace of the sinkhole (no route out).
limits: Install ran in a separate container with unrestricted network access (to fetch the package), with install scripts and source builds disabled.
File reads are not recorded; writes are measured against the freshly installed image.
Writes to tmpfs mounts such as /dev/shm are not visible.
Only tools declared read-only (or named with --safe-tool) were called, with synthetic inputs; every other tool's behaviour is unobserved.
Effects are attributed to the phase in which they appeared; background activity can land in a neighbouring phase.
One short session was observed; delayed or conditional behaviour may not have triggered.
Rewrites of files already changed in an earlier phase are detected by size and modification time while the server runs; a rewrite that keeps both, or one during shutdown, is not seen.
Non-DNS UDP is counted without its destination.

headline: No mismatches observed in the sandbox. That is evidence, not a guarantee.

suggestions.title: Pinned launch entry
suggestions.note: Generated from published metadata with the exact version. MCPAudit never reads or edits your client configuration; paste it yourself after review.

suggestions.title: Tool permissions (Claude Code settings)
suggestions.note: allow: declared read-only and called successfully with no effects seen. deny: declared destructive, injection-matching, or a high-severity mismatch. ask: everything not proven either way.

suggestions.title: Network egress
suggestions.note: Hosts are attempts recorded by the sinkhole; none were reached. Allow only what the tools you use need.

suggestions.title: Filesystem writes
suggestions.note: Paths are where it wrote during the observed session; reads were not recorded.
